ideas.title: Climb anything: a grab that can slip
ideas.goal: as Lumi the player jumps at a wall and catches whatever lip the claws reach; whether it holds comes from how they arrive (speed, angle) and from the shape of the lip, never from a tag. Fun because the island becomes a climbing route you read with your own eyes, and a bad grab is a real fall you can see coming.
ideas.idea: No grab animation and no per-material dice. Lumi is a PrintSim affine body flying on its jump; the claws are two contact points that meet a lip found on the real mesh by climb.jl (every lip up a wall since s135, with its top normal and the curvature of the edge read from the probe rays). Every substep the solver asks the contact for the force that keeps the claw on the lip; the claw holds only while that force lies inside the friction cone around the lip's local normal (|f_t| <= mu f_n). Arrive fast and the impulse is mostly tangential: the claws skid along the lip, leaving the cone, and the same body falls. On a rounded beam the normal tips away as the claw slides, so the cone shrinks under it until it lets go: geometry decides, not a tag. I measure the threshold (approach speed at which the shelf stops holding) and film two jumps at the same wall, one under it and one over it.
ideas.form: physics/climb.jl + PrintSim contact + jump-in plugin (jump at a wall); traced film side-on and close: one hold, one slip, same wall, speeds on the caption

ideas.title: Tippe top duel in a wooden bowl
ideas.goal: the player and a friend each pull the string on a top into a shallow wooden bowl; the bowl's slope drives the tops together, they clash and trade spin, and the one still spinning wins. The strange round top can rise onto its stem mid-fight and becomes almost impossible to knock over. Fun because the pull (how hard, how tilted, where in the bowl) is a skill, the clashes are loud and fast, and the flip is a trick you learn to set up.
ideas.idea: Each top is a rigid body with sliding friction against the bowl's real mesh and against the other tops: precession, nutation, the wobble as spin bleeds off, spin traded through friction at each clash, and the tippe top inverting purely from friction torque on its offset centre of mass (a textbook rigid-body result). The string pull sets the initial spin and tilt from the player's input. Someone watching sees two tops circle down the bowl, spark off each other, and the round one stand up on its stem and keep going.
ideas.form: rigid bodies with friction contact (PrintSim affine bodies on Mantle) + a bowl asset + a two-player mini game; traced film at bowl height
